items.title: Total charge, dipole moment, Cartesian moments and traceless quadrupole of a static charge distribution
items.statement:
For the Lebesgue branches (a),(b), assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the exact measure interface ([[def-countable-choice]]). The finite moment sums in branch(c) are defined and computed without Choice. Let the laboratory region, its chart, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\delta_{ij}$ be the Kronecker symbol in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame, with $|y|$ the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. This definition assigns **source moments** to a static charge distribution in the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (d) and (e). Two branches are declared.

(a) [Absolutely continuous branch] Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real ([[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]) and vanish $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere outside the closed ball $\overline B_a(0)=\{y:|y|\le a\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]). The **total charge** $Q$, the **dipole moment** $p$, the **degree-$l$ Cartesian moments** $M_{i_1\dots i_l}$ and the **traceless quadrupole** $Q_{ij}$ are
$$Q:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\,d\lambda_3,\qquad p_i:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}y_i\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
$$M_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\quad(l\ge0),\qquad Q_{ij}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\bigl(3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
with $M^{(0)}:=Q$ and $M_i:=p_i$, indices in $\{1,2,3\}$, units C, C m, C m$^l$ and C m$^2$, and integrals in the sense of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]] and [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. Each integral is absolutely convergent: since $\rho=0$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. off $\overline B_a(0)$ and the maps $y\mapsto y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}$ and $y\mapsto 3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}$ are bounded there by $a^l$ and $4a^2$, the integrands are dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by $a^l|\rho|$ and $4a^2|\rho|$, which lie in $L^1$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). The traceless quadrupole is traceless, $\sum_iQ_{ii}=0$, since $\sum_i(3y_i^2-|y|^2)=0$ pointwise ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]), and replacing $\rho$ by an equal $\lambda_3$-a.e. density changes no moment ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]).

(b) [General locally integrable branch] If instead $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$ is real and $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^l|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)<\infty$ for a given integer $l\ge0$, then the degree-$l$ Cartesian moments of the same formula are absolutely convergent and defined; if the absolute weighted moment $\int |y|^L|\rho(y)|dy$ is finite for any real $L\ge0$, then every integer Cartesian degree $0\le l\le L$ is defined. The convention $|y|^0=1$ includes the origin. No compact support and no $L^1$-membership is assumed in this branch.

(c) [Finite system of stationary point charges] Let $N\ge0$, $x_1,\dots,x_N\in\mathbb R^3$ and $q_1,\dots,q_N\in\mathbb R$ be charge parameters ([[def-em-sources]] (a)), read as the stationary point charges $q_k\delta_{x_k}$ in the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e). Define
$$Q:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k,\qquad p:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_kx_k,\qquad M_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k\,x_{k,i_1}\cdots x_{k,i_l},\qquad Q_{ij}:=\sum_{k=1}^Nq_k\bigl(3x_{k,i}x_{k,j}-|x_k|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr),$$
finite sums in the sense of [[def-finite-sum]] ([[lem-finite-sum-laws]]); again $\sum_iQ_{ii}=0$. The points need not be distinct; charges at a common point add.

(d) [Reference point and scope] Every moment is computed about the chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; this origin is part of the definition. These are source moments of a prescribed static distribution — not momenta, rest masses, intrinsic spins, self-energies or dynamical quantities — and no field, force, equation of motion, equilibrium or empirical claim is made here; the static regime in which the source is read is the adopted idealisation of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (f). Every Cartesian degree l in this definition is a nonnegative integer (the number of Cartesian indices); only the absolute weighted exponent L in(b) may be any nonnegative real number.
items.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition with its well-definedness checks displayed in the clauses: absolute convergence and null-set irrelevance in (a), the finite-absolute-moment hypothesis in (b), and the finite-sum identities in (c). The mathematical inputs are the Lebesgue interface ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]), the pointwise bounds $|y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}|\le a^l$ and $|3y_iy_j-|y|^2\delta_{ij}|\le4a^2$ on $\overline B_a(0)$, the triangle and monotonicity estimates ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]), linearity of the integral ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]), null-set irrelevance ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]) and finite-sum algebra ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]). The physical reading uses only the fixed-time dictionary of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (d), (e); no Choice beyond the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the measure interface is used. For branch (b), local integrability on the compact closed unit ball gives $\int_{|y|\le1}|\rho|<\infty$. For a real $L\ge0$ and integer $0\le l\le L$, on that ball $|y|^l\le1$, while on $|y|>1$ one has $|y|^l\le|y|^L$. Split the nonnegative integral into these two measurable sets and use [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]: $\int|y|^l|\rho|\le\int_{|y|\le1}|\rho|+\int_{|y|>1}|y|^L|\rho|<\infty$. Cartesian monomials of degree l have modulus at most |y|^l, so all lower moments exist, including Q at l0. Thus L1 follows as a consequence, not as an added hypothesis. The finite-point algebra in (c) is choice-free independent of the Lebesgue branches. The unit-ball split uses numerical coordinates in the fixed SI chart. Equivalently for any chosen radius Rstar>0 one obtains the dimensionally explicit bound $\int|y|^l|\rho|\le R_\ast^l\int_{|y|\le R_\ast}|\rho|+R_\ast^{l-L}\int_{|y|>R_\ast}|y|^L|\rho|$, with Rstar set to the coordinate unit radius in the preceding proof.

items.physical_scope: Source moments (total charge, dipole moment, Cartesian moments, traceless quadrupole) of a prescribed static charge distribution read at fixed time in one named inertial frame: an absolutely continuous compactly supported $L^1$ density, a locally integrable density with a finite absolute moment of the stated order, or a finite system of stationary point charges. These are kinematic source characteristics: no field, force, dynamics, self-energy, stability or empirical content is asserted, and the static regime is an adopted idealisation. In the noncompact locally integrable branch a finite weighted absolute moment may have any real exponent L>=0 and supplies every integer Cartesian degree<=L by the local unit-ball and outer weighted estimate; L1 is a conclusion, not an added hypothesis. Finite moment-sum algebra is choice-free.

items.title: Origin shift of the source moments: $Q$, the dipole $p-Qb$, the Cartesian expansion and the traceless quadrupole
items.statement:
For the density-integral branch assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) through the Lebesgue interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); the finite-point branch of all identities below is choice-free. Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and vanish $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$, or let $(x_k,q_k)_{k=1}^N$ be a finite system of stationary point charges, with the source moments of [[def-em-electric-moments]] branches (a) and (c) respectively. For $b\in\mathbb R^3$ define the moments **about the reference point $b$** by replacing, in each integrand of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a) and in each summand of (c), the vector $y$ by $y-b$ (respectively $x_k$ by $x_k-b$):
$$Q^{(b)}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\,d\lambda_3,\quad p^{(b)}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(y-b)\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),\quad M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\prod_{r=1}^l(y-b)_{i_r}\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
$$Q^{(b)}_{ij}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\bigl(3(y-b)_i(y-b)_j-|y-b|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
and analogously with finite sums $M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}=\sum_{k=1}^N q_k\prod_{r=1}^l(x_k-b)_{i_r}$ in the point-charge branch. Every displayed integral is absolutely convergent: $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support the monomials obey $|y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_l}|\le a^l$ and, for $y-b$, $|y-b|^l\le(|y|+|b|)^l$ and $|3(y-b)_i(y-b)_j-|y-b|^2\delta_{ij}|\le4(|y|+|b|)^2$, so the integrands are dominated by constants times $|\rho|\in L^1$ ([[def-em-electric-moments]] (a), [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Then:
(a) $Q^{(b)}=Q$ for every $b$;
(b) $p^{(b)}=p-Qb$, so the dipole moment is independent of the reference point exactly when $Q=0$;
(c) for every $l\ge0$,
$$M^{(b)}_{i_1\dots i_l}=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,l\}}(-1)^{|S|}\Bigl(\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}\Bigr)M_{(i_r:\,r\notin S)},$$
where $M_{(i_r:\,r\notin S)}$ is the Cartesian moment whose index list is the complement of $S$ and the empty index list is read as $Q$; in particular
$$M^{(b)}_{ij}=M_{ij}-b_ip_j-b_jp_i+b_ib_jQ;$$
(d) $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=Q_{ij}-3\bigl(b_ip_j+b_jp_i\bigr)+2(b\cdot p)\delta_{ij}+\bigl(3b_ib_j-|b|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)Q$; consequently, if $Q=0$ and $p=0$, then $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=Q_{ij}$ for every $b$ (the traceless quadrupole of a neutral, non-dipolar distribution is independent of the reference point);
(e) [Scope] this is an exact identity between the declared source moments of [[def-em-electric-moments]]; it asserts nothing about fields, forces, dynamics or nature, and the reference point is a choice of coordinate origin, not an operation performed on the source.
items.strategy:
The theorem is the expansion of the polynomial $\prod_{r=1}^l(y_{i_r}-b_{i_r})$ followed by termwise integration (or summation). For (a) and (b) the degrees $0$ and $1$ are immediate; constant multiples of $\rho$ and of $y_i\rho$ pass through the integral by linearity of the Lebesgue integral on $L^1$ ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]), and the finite-sum branch by linearity of finite sums ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]). For (c), expand by finite distributivity,
$$\prod_{r=1}^l(y_{i_r}-b_{i_r})=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,l\}}(-1)^{|S|}\Bigl(\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}\Bigr)\Bigl(\prod_{r\notin S}y_{i_r}\Bigr),$$
an identity of real polynomials proved by induction on $l$ (finitely many distribution steps, [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the polynomial calculus), and integrate term by term: each complement monomial in the term indexed by S is dominated $\lambda_3$-a.e. by $a^{l-|S|}|\rho|$, and its fixed coefficient has modulus $\prod_{r\in S}|b_{i_r}|$. A common envelope for all finitely many expanded terms is $(1+a+|b|)^l|\rho|$ on the support, hence absolutely integrable by [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a), so the finitely many applications of linearity are legitimate and the constants $\prod_{r\in S}b_{i_r}$ factor out ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). For (d), multiply the case $l=2$ by $3$ and subtract $\delta_{ij}\sum_kM^{(b)}_{kk}$, using $Q^{(b)}_{ij}=3M^{(b)}_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kM^{(b)}_{kk}$, $Q_{ij}=3M_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kM_{kk}$ and $\sum_kM^{(b)}_{kk}=\sum_kM_{kk}-2b\cdot p+|b|^2Q$; this gives the displayed identity, and its four $b$-dependent terms vanish identically when $Q=0$ and $p=0$. Replacing $\rho$ by an equal $\lambda_3$-a.e. density changes no integral ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]). The finite-sum branch repeats the same algebra with sums. No Choice beyond the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used; (e) records the scope.

items.physical_scope: The exact reference-point dependence of the source moments of a static charge distribution: Q is reference-point independent, the dipole moment shifts by -Qb, every Cartesian moment has the displayed subset expansion, and the traceless quadrupole is reference-point independent for a neutral, non-dipolar distribution. The claim is a moment identity, not a statement about fields, forces, dynamics or empirical fact.

items.title: External force and torque on a small neutral charge distribution in a slowly varying electrostatic field
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the Lebesgue interface ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and vanish $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$; let $E_{\mathrm{ext}}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be a prescribed external vector-field datum, with electric-field units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] that is continuous on $\overline B_a(0)$ and Lipschitz there with constant $L\ge0$, i.e. $|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(x)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(x')|\le L|x-x'|$ for all $x,x'\in\overline B_a(0)$. Consider the matter model in which the prescribed static distribution $\rho$ is carried by a body at rest in the laboratory frame and adopt additionally the prescribed external force model $f_{\mathrm{ext}}=\rho E_{\mathrm{ext}}$. This is a declared extension to these locally integrable charge data and Lipschitz fields, motivated by the smooth continuum coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (ii); that postulate covers smooth sources and does not itself establish this extension. The only force counted by the present model is $f_{\mathrm{ext}}$; the self-field of $\rho$, all other fields, mechanical support and back-reaction are excluded by this model. Define the **total external force** and the **total external torque about the origin** by the componentwise Lebesgue integrals
$$F:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)\,E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\in\mathbb R^3,\qquad \tau:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)\,\bigl(y\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)\bigr)\,d\lambda_3(y)\in\mathbb R^3,$$
absolutely convergent because on the support $|E_{\mathrm{ext}}|\le|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|+La$ and $|y\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}|\le a(|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|+La)$, so each component is dominated by a constant times $|\rho|\in L^1$ ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[thm-cross-product-norm-is-the-two-vector-gram-determinant]], [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Then:
(a) [Uniform force and torque expansions]
$$F=Q\,E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+R_F,\qquad |R_F|\le L\,a\,\|\rho\|_1,\qquad \tau=p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+R_\tau,\qquad |R_\tau|\le L\,a^2\|\rho\|_1,$$
where $Q$ and $p$ are the total charge and dipole moment of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a) and $\|\rho\|_1=\int|\rho|\,d\lambda_3$;
(b) [Neutral distribution] if $Q=0$ then the leading force term vanishes, $F=R_F$ with $|R_F|\le La\|\rho\|_1$, and the torque is the ideal-dipole torque $p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ up to the bound $|R_\tau|\le La^2\|\rho\|_1$; in this sense a neutral distribution of size $a$ in a field with Lipschitz constant $L$ carries the dipole torque $p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ with an explicit remainder;
(c) [Reference-point shift] for any reference point $o\in\mathbb R^3$, the torque about $o$, $\tau_o:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)\,(y-o)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)$, equals $\tau-o\times F$ exactly;
(d) [Ideal pair of test charges at rest] let $q\in\mathbb R$ and $d\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, put $a=|d|/2$, and consider the two stationary point charges $+q$ at $d/2$ and $-q$ at $-d/2$ ([[def-em-electric-moments]] (c)), each treated as a test charge at rest in the laboratory chart in the same prescribed external field $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, with the mutual interaction and the self-field of each charge excluded by the model. Adopt for this finite prescribed-charge branch the external force assignment $F_k=q_kE_{\rm ext}(x_k)$ and torque $x_k\times F_k$. It is defined for merely continuous external field values at the two points, independently of a worldline equation. For the same Lipschitz bound as above, finite summation gives the expansions of (a),(b), with Q0, p=qd, and total variation2|q|: $|R_F|\le2|q|La$, $|R_\tau|\le2|q|La^2$. More generally the exact finite force/torque sum requires only the specified field values; no Lipschitz estimate is asserted without its hypothesis.

(d1) [Covariant sufficient specialization] If, in addition, an actual prescribed electromagnetic tensor $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of each massive future-timelike $C^2$ test worldline with constant charge qprime and supplied rest mass m>0, and the external-field coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](i) applies, then at an instant with zero coordinate velocity $U=(c,0,0,0)$ its spatial force is $q'E_{\rm ext}$, because $U_0=-c$ and $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$. This reproduces the prescribed point-force assignment at that instant. Similarly the smooth-source $J=0$ matter-coupling branch of postulate(ii) reproduces the continuum force assignment when its own source/field/matter hypotheses hold. No C1 tensor or worldline is inferred from merely continuous E data, and no two-charge trajectory existence or permanent rest is claimed.

(e) [Scope] the statement is conditional on the explicitly stated matter model: only the prescribed external field acts on the distribution, the distribution is prescribed and at rest, and no self-force, back-reaction, mechanical equilibrium, stability or dynamics of the body is asserted; the external field is a datum, not solved for. Clause (d) is an instantaneous idealisation of two ideal point test charges with mutual interaction excluded; it is not a two-body dynamics, a bound-state or a stability statement. No radiation, medium response or empirical claim is made. The prescribed finite force assignment and finite moment algebra in(d) are choice-free; the volume integrals in(a)-(c) carry their explicit measure premise, while(d1) is a separate conditional instantiation of the exact physical coupling.
items.strategy: Write $E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)=E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)+\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support and integrate term by term. For (a), the constant term of the force gives $\bigl(\int\rho\,d\lambda_3\bigr)E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)=QE_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$, and the constant term of the torque gives $\bigl(\int\rho(y)\,y\,d\lambda_3(y)\bigr)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)=p\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)$ by linearity of the integral on $L^1$ and the bilinearity of the cross product ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). For the force remainder, if $R_F\ne0$ test it against the unit vector $u:=R_F/|R_F|$: $|R_F|=u\cdot R_F=\int\rho(y)\,u\cdot\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)d\lambda_3(y)\le\int|\rho(y)|\,|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le L\int|y|\,|\rho(y)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le La\|\rho\|_1$, using $u\cdot v\le|v|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), the triangle and monotonicity rules for the integral ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) and $|y|\le a$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support; the case $R_F=0$ is trivial. For the torque remainder, $\bigl|\int\rho(y)\,y\times\bigl(E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)\bigr)d\lambda_3(y)\bigr|\le\int|\rho(y)|\,|y|\,|E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)-E_{\mathrm{ext}}(0)|\,d\lambda_3(y)\le L\int|y|^2|\rho|\,d\lambda_3\le La^2\|\rho\|_1$, using $|y\times v|\le|y|\,|v|$ ([[thm-cross-product-norm-is-the-two-vector-gram-determinant]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Since the two integrals are absolutely convergent, all interchanges are finitely many applications of linearity and the triangle rule. For (b) insert $Q=0$. For (c), subtract and add $o$: $\int\rho(y)(y-o)\times E_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)d\lambda_3=\tau-o\times F$ by linearity and bilinearity of the cross product. For (d), under the explicitly adopted point-force assignment sum the two forces q E(d/2) and -q E(-d/2) and their position cross products. Finite bilinearity gives p=qd and the same estimates as(a), replacing the density integral by the finite sum and its total variation2|q|. This algebra uses only the actual field values and the Lipschitz assumption for the numerical error bounds, not an unstated C1 regularity premise. For(d1), when the additional C1 prescribed tensor and massive C2-worldline hypotheses explicitly hold, the exact Lorentz postulate gives $m dU^i/d\tau=q'F^{i0}U_0=q'(-E_i/c)(-c)=q'E_i$ at rest, using the cited tensor/worldline conventions. This is an instantaneous sufficient instantiation only. The smooth continuum branch likewise reproduces rho E only under its explicit smooth-source matter-coupling hypotheses; the broader L1/Lipschitz model is separately adopted. Clause (e) records the model assumptions. Countable Choice is used only through the Lebesgue integrals and their suppliers; the Lipschitz constant and the field values enter only through the displayed estimates, and the norm continuity of [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]] is used to read the pointwise bounds. Changing $\rho$ on a $\lambda_3$-null set changes no integral ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]).

items.physical_scope: Prescribed external force and torque for broad compact L1 charge data and a Lipschitz external vector-field datum under an explicitly additional rho E force model, with full force/torque/origin-shift bounds. A separate finite point-force assignment needs only external values (continuity for the stated field datum); its Lipschitz bounds are retained. Exact Lorentz-postulate instantiation is restricted explicitly to its smooth-source matter branch or C1 prescribed tensor and massive C2 test-worldline hypotheses at an instant of rest. No self-force, trajectory existence, permanent rest, equilibrium, stability or empirical assertion is supplied.

items.title: Uniform Coulomb dipole expansion of a compactly supported charge density with an explicit remainder
items.strategy: First, for $|x|\ge2a$ and $\lambda_3$-a.e. $y$ one has $\rho(y)=0$ off $\overline B_a(0)$, while for $y\in\overline B_a(0)$ one has $|x-y|\ge r-a\ge r/2>0$ ([[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); hence $|x-y|^{-1}\le2/r$ on the support and the integral against $\rho$ converges absolutely ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Since the kernel is bounded on the support and the support is $\lambda_3$-a.e. contained in $\overline B_a(0)$, the unnormalised integral equals $4\pi N\rho(x)$ by the defining formula of [[def-newtonian-potential]] ([[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]). Because $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)$ for $n=3$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (c)), one has $N\rho(x)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)|x-y|^{-1}\,d\lambda_3(y)$ and hence $\varphi(x)=(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)|x-y|^{-1}\,d\lambda_3(y)$ for $r\ge2a$. The monopole-dipole splitting of [[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]] applied with the same $a$ gives $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y)|x-y|^{-1}\,d\lambda_3(y)=Q/r+p\cdot x/r^3+R_0(x)$ with $|R_0(x)|\le16a^2\|\rho\|_1/r^3$ for all $r\ge2a$; multiplying the identity by the constant $(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}$ (linearity of the integral on $L^1$, [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]) gives (a) with $R:=(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}R_0$ and the displayed bound $|R(x)|\le16a^2\|\rho\|_1/(4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3)$. Nothing at $r<2a$ is asserted, because the kernel singularity may meet the support there; the proof uses no differentiation of the remainder. For (b), $|p\cdot x|\le|p|\,|x|$ by Cauchy-Schwarz for the Euclidean inner product ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), so $|p\cdot x|/r^3\le|p|/r^2$, and the triangle inequality for the modulus completes the estimate. For (c), the regularity, the harmonicity off $\overline B_a(0)$ and the identity $-\Delta T_\varphi=T_{\rho/\varepsilon_0}$ are exactly [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (c), whose potential is already $\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$; no second scaling by $\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ is applied; the fixed-time dictionary between the spatial equations and the weak four-dimensional reading is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e); in the smooth branch the pointwise equations and the field $E=-\nabla\varphi$ are those of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (a) ([[def-em-fields]] for the field object).

items.physical_scope: The exterior potential of a compactly supported $L^1$ charge density in classical electrostatics: for $|x|\ge2a$ the localised Newtonian potential equals the monopole term plus the dipole term plus an explicit remainder bounded by $16a^2\|\rho\|_1/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3)$, uniformly in the exterior region. Only the potential is expanded; no derivative estimate of the remainder, no field expansion and no value on or inside the support are claimed.

items.title: Convergent all-order spherical multipole expansion with monopole, dipole and quadrupole terms
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, spherical-harmonic and Newtonian interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and vanish $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$ ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); let $Q$, $p$ and $Q_{ij}$ be the total charge, dipole moment and traceless quadrupole of $\rho$ about the chart origin ([[def-em-electric-moments]] (a)); let $\varphi:=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ be the potential of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (c) with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; and let $\{Y_{lm}:l\ge0,\ m=1,\dots,2l+1\}$ be a real orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics of $L^2(S^2,d\sigma)$ of degree $l$, with $d\sigma$ the surface measure of total mass $4\pi$ and the addition theorem of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]] ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). For every $l,m$ define the **spherical multipole moment of degree $l$**
$$q_{lm}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^l\,Y_{lm}(y/|y|)\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
absolutely convergent because $|Y_{lm}|\le((2l+1)/(4\pi))^{1/2}$ on $S^2$ by the addition theorem and $|y|\le a$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support, so the integrand is dominated by $a^l((2l+1)/(4\pi))^{1/2}|\rho|$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Write $x=rn$ with $r=|x|$ and $n\in S^2$. Then:
(a) [Exterior spherical multipole expansion] for every $x$ with $r>a$,
$$\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{l=0}^{\infty}\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\,\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}\,q_{lm},$$
the series converging absolutely and uniformly on $\{|x|\ge r_0\}$ for every $r_0>a$, with the tail after degree $N$ bounded by
$$\Bigl\|\,\varphi-\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{l=0}^{N}\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}q_{lm}\Bigr\|_{\infty,\{|x|\ge r_0\}}\le\frac{\|\rho\|_1\,a^{N+1}}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\,r_0^{N+2}\,(1-a/r_0)};$$
(b) [Monopole, dipole and quadrupole terms] the degree-$0$ and degree-$1$ terms of (a) are the monopole and dipole terms $Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0r)$ and $p\cdot x/(4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3)$, and for $r\ge2a$ the difference between $\varphi$ and the truncation after degree $1$ obeys the remainder bound of [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]]; the degree-$2$ term equals the traceless-quadrupole term
$$\frac{1}{8\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}\,n_iQ_{ij}n_j;$$
(c) [Regularity and termwise differentiation] $\varphi$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\{|x|>a\}$, the series in (a) may be differentiated termwise to every order, the differentiated series converging uniformly on every compact subset of $\{|x|>a\}$; in particular the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ of [[def-em-fields]] equals $-\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{l,m}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\nabla_x\bigl(Y_{lm}(n)r^{-l-1}\bigr)q_{lm}$ on $\{|x|>a\}$, with the same uniform convergence on compact subsets;
(d) [Scope of exterior clauses (a)-(c)] those clauses concern a real compactly supported $L^1$ density and the exterior region $r>a$; they make no claim on or inside $\overline B_a(0)$, no convergence at $r=a$ is asserted, the exterior-density expansion is not asserted for point or singular sources, and no empirical content is involved. The expansion is the exterior expansion of the potential of the static source $\rho$ read in the fixed-time dictionary of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e).

(e) [Separate source-free ball boundary branch] Let R>0 be a radius and let real f in $L^2(S^2,d\sigma)$ be prescribed scalar-potential boundary data (unit V) on the sphere x=Rn, with $f_{lm}=\int_{S^2}fY_{lm}d\sigma$. Independently of the exterior density rho, define on |x|<R
$$\varphi_f(rn)=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}(r/R)^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n),$$
with the constant degree-zero value at r0. Then this is smooth and harmonic in the ball; its series and every derivative converge uniformly on every smaller closed ball, $\sup_{0\le t<1}\|\varphi_f(Rt\,\cdot)\|_2\le\|f\|_2$, and $\varphi_f(Rt\,\cdot)\to f$ in L2 as t tends1. It is the unique harmonic scalar potential in the class with bounded radial L2 norm and that L2 boundary limit. With $E_f=-\nabla\varphi_f$, $B=0$, $\rho=J=0$ and time-independent fields, this gives a full source-free electrostatic Maxwell model inside the ball under [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. For continuous f the same potential is
$$\varphi_f(x)=\int_{S^2}\frac{1-|x|^2/R^2}{4\pi|x/R-n'|^3}f(n')\,d\sigma(n'),$$
and it extends continuously to the closed ball with value f(n) at Rn; the angular Poisson kernel is positive of mass one. No boundary value or boundary electric-field trace for the exterior arbitrary-L1 density is inferred, and no derivative boundary regularity for arbitrary f is asserted. In every coefficient integral the factor $|y|^lY_{lm}(y/|y|)$ is defined at y0 by its homogeneous polynomial extension: zero for l>=1 and the constant degree-zero harmonic for l0. This is a finite assignment, and changing its value at that null singleton changes no integral.
items.strategy:
Scale the spherical multipole expansion of [[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]] (a)-(b) by the constant $(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}$, exactly as in [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]]: since $N\rho(x)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int\rho(y)|x-y|^{-1}d\lambda_3(y)$ for the observation points considered, $\varphi=(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}\int\rho(y)|x-y|^{-1}d\lambda_3(y)$, and part (a) of the supplier gives the displayed series, its absolute and uniform convergence on exterior regions, and the stated tail bound, all multiplied by the constant $(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}$ ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]] for scaling the integral, [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). The coefficients $q_{lm}$ are absolutely convergent by the addition theorem's bound $\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}Y_{lm}(n)^2=(2l+1)/(4\pi)$ of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]], which gives $|Y_{lm}|\le((2l+1)/(4\pi))^{1/2}$, and by $|y|\le a$ on the support ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). For (b): the degree-$0$ and degree-$1$ identifications and the remainder bound are parts of the supplier's clause (a) (with $Q=\int\rho$, $p=\int y\rho(y)d\lambda_3(y)$ and the bound $16a^2\|\rho\|_1/|x|^3$ for $|x|\ge2a$), scaled by $(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^{-1}$, and they reproduce [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]] (a). For the degree-$2$ term, use the addition theorem at $l=2$: $\sum_mY_{2m}(n)Y_{2m}(y/|y|)=\frac{5}{4\pi}P_2(n\cdot y/|y|)$, so that
$$\sum_{m=1}^{5}Y_{2m}(n)q_{2m}=\frac{5}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^2P_2\Bigl(n\cdot\frac{y}{|y|}\Bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$
and the second Legendre polynomial is fixed by the defining identity $(1-2qz+q^2)^{-1/2}=\sum_{l\ge0}q^lP_l(z)$ of [[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]: the coefficient of $q^2$ in the Taylor expansion of the left side at $q=0$ is $\frac12\frac{d^2}{dq^2}(1-2qz+q^2)^{-1/2}\big|_{q=0}=\frac{3z^2-1}{2}$ (the first and second derivatives computed by the chain rule, [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]), while that coefficient on the right side is $P_2(z)$ (uniqueness of Taylor coefficients, [[def-taylor-polynomial-and-remainder]], [[lem-taylor-polynomial-derivatives]]); hence $P_2(z)=(3z^2-1)/2$. Therefore $|y|^2P_2(n\cdot y/|y|)=\bigl(3(n\cdot y)^2-|y|^2\bigr)/2$, and
$$\sum_{m=1}^{5}Y_{2m}(n)q_{2m}=\frac{5}{8\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\bigl(3(n\cdot y)^2-|y|^2\bigr)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)=\frac{5}{8\pi}\,n_iQ_{ij}n_j$$
by the definition of $Q_{ij}$ in [[def-em-electric-moments]] (a) and linearity of the integral; the degree-$2$ term of (a) is then $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\cdot\frac{4\pi}{5}\cdot\frac{1}{r^3}\cdot\frac{5}{8\pi}n_iQ_{ij}n_j=\frac{n_iQ_{ij}n_j}{8\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}$. For (c): part (b) of [[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]] gives that $\varphi$ is $C^\infty$ on $\{|x|>a\}$ and that the series may be differentiated termwise to every order with uniform convergence of each differentiated series on compact subsets; the displayed field series is the termwise gradient, with [[def-em-fields]] for the field object. The fixed-time dictionary is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e). All estimates use the triangle and monotonicity rules for the Lebesgue integral ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]), the $\lambda_3$-a.e. support convention ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]], [[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]) and the declared Countable Choice of the measure, harmonic and Newtonian interfaces; no convergence at $r=a$ and no point-source assertion is made. For(e), apply [[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]](c), equivalently [[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]], to f in the unit variable z=x/R. The scaling gives exactly (r/R)^l, preserves the stated radial L2 norm/limit, and multiplies a derivative of order alpha by R^(-|alpha|), so every smaller-ball derivative convergence and uniqueness follows. For continuous f the same substitution yields the displayed angular Poisson kernel with total mass one; no accidental factor R² is introduced since integration is on the unit sphere. Harmonicity gives div E_f=-Delta phi_f0 and smooth mixed-derivative cancellation gives curl E_f0 via [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]. B and all time/source terms vanish, proving all four adopted equations inside the ball. The branch has independent boundary datum f and no density rho in that ball; it restores the approved H3 content without a false trace conclusion at the exterior support radius a.

items.title: Four stationary point charges with vanishing total charge and dipole moment and traceless quadrupole diag(6qa^2,-6qa^2,0)
items.strategy: Insert the four points into the finite sums of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c) and use $\delta$-orthonormality of the frame basis: $Q=q+q-q-q=0$ and $p=q(ae_1)+q(-ae_1)+(-q)(ae_2)+(-q)(-ae_2)=0$. For (a), the configuration is invariant under $x\mapsto-x$ with the charge of each point preserved ($+q$ at $\pm ae_1$ and $-q$ at $\pm ae_2$), so pairing each point with its image and reindexing the finite sum ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]) gives $M_{i_1\dots i_{2k+1}}=\sum_k q_k x_k^{\otimes(2k+1)}=0$: the terms at $x$ and $-x$ contribute $q\bigl(1+(-1)^{2k+1}\bigr)x^{\otimes(2k+1)}=0$. For (b), direct substitution gives $M_{ij}=q(ae_1)_i(ae_1)_j+q(-ae_1)_i(-ae_1)_j-q(ae_2)_i(ae_2)_j-q(-ae_2)_i(-ae_2)_j=2qa^2\bigl(e_{1i}e_{1j}-e_{2i}e_{2j}\bigr)=2qa^2\bigl(\delta_{i1}\delta_{j1}-\delta_{i2}\delta_{j2}\bigr)$, whose trace $2qa^2(1-1)$ vanishes; the components are read in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). For (c), use $Q_{ij}=\sum_kq_k\bigl(3x_{k,i}x_{k,j}-|x_k|^2\delta_{ij}\bigr)=3M_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kq_k|x_k|^2$ from [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c); each $|x_k|=a$, so $\sum_kq_k|x_k|^2=a^2(q+q-q-q)=0$ and $Q_{ij}=3M_{ij}=6qa^2\bigl(\delta_{i1}\delta_{j1}-\delta_{i2}\delta_{j2}\bigr)$, with trace $6qa^2(1-1)=0$; the reference-point independence for $Q=p=0$ is clause (d) of [[pthm-em-moment-origin-change]]. The equality $|x_k|=a$ for $x_k=\pm ae_1,\pm ae_2$ uses $\delta(e_r,e_r)=1$ ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]) and the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (with [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]] for reading norms of coordinate vectors). Clause (d) records that no field, energy or dynamics is computed. No Choice axiom is used: all sums are finite ([[lem-finite-sum-laws]]).

items.title: Exact two-charge dipole potential, its moments and the explicit far-field remainder
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited distribution and Lebesgue interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $q\in\mathbb R$ and $d\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, put $a:=|d|/2$, and let the source be the two stationary point charges $+q$ at $d/2$ and $-q$ at $-d/2$ (charge parameters in coulombs and the constant $\varepsilon_0$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]), with fixed-time reading $q\delta_{d/2}-q\delta_{-d/2}$ ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e), [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]). Define, with arbitrary values at the two points,
$$\varphi(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-d/2|}-\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x+d/2|}\qquad\bigl(x\notin\{d/2,-d/2\}\bigr).$$
Then:
(a) [Exact potential and equations] $\varphi$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ and of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{d/2,-d/2\}$; with $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ on that set ([[def-em-fields]]), the pair $(E,0)$ satisfies the distributional pure electrostatic equations
$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{q\,\delta_{d/2}-q\,\delta_{-d/2}}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$
of the fixed-time dictionary of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e) ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) for each point charge, added by linearity of distributional differentiation: [[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]);
(b) [Moments] in the finite-sum branch of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c) about the chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], $Q=0$, $p=qd$, every even Cartesian moment vanishes, $M_{i_1\dots i_{2k+1}}=2q\,(d/2)_{i_1}\cdots(d/2)_{i_{2k+1}}$ for every $k\ge0$, and the traceless quadrupole vanishes, $Q_{ij}=0$;
(c) [Exact far-field comparison] for every $x$ with $r:=|x|\ge2a=|d|$, the exact difference obeys the expansion form of [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]] with the point-pair total variation in place of $\|\rho\|_1$:
$$\varphi(x)=\frac{p\cdot x}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}+R(x),\qquad |R(x)|\le\frac{16\,a^2\,(|q|+|{-q}|)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}=\frac{8|q|a^2}{\pi\varepsilon_0r^3};$$
(d) [Comparison with the compact-density theorem] the hypothesis of [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]] is an $L^1$ density and is not met by the point pair, so that theorem is not applied to it; the identity and bound of (c) are proved directly for the two kernels by the twice-fundamental-theorem computation used in that theorem's remainder, and the leading term, the $a^2$ decay and the appearance of the total variation agree with the compact-density expansion;
(e) [Scope] the potential and the distributional equations are stated for the idealised singular source; no self-energy, self-force, dynamics, bound-state, stability or empirical claim is made for the pair. The vanishing quadrupole in (b) is about the specified symmetric origin only; at a general reference point b its value is $-3(b_i p_j+b_jp_i)+2(b\cdot p)\delta_{ij}$, since Q0.
items.strategy:
The individual point-charge objects and their distributional identities are those of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d): for a charge $q'$ at $x_0$, $\varphi_{q'}$ is locally integrable, $C^\infty$ off $x_0$, $E_{q'}=-\nabla\varphi_{q'}$ off $x_0$, and $\operatorname{div}E_{q'}=(q'/\varepsilon_0)\delta_{x_0}$, $\operatorname{curl}E_{q'}=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$. Summing the two locally integrable potentials gives the displayed $\varphi$ (values at the two points are immaterial, [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], [[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]), and the distributional derivative of the sum is the sum of the distributional derivatives ([[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], [[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); adding the two point-charge identities componentwise and using [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]] gives (a), and the fixed-time dictionary is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e). For (b), substitute into the finite sums of [[def-em-electric-moments]] (c): $Q=q+(-q)=0$, $p=q(d/2)+(-q)(-d/2)=qd$, and $M_{i_1\dots i_l}=q(d/2)^{\otimes l}+(-q)(-d/2)^{\otimes l}=q\bigl(1-(-1)^l\bigr)(d/2)^{\otimes l}$, which vanishes for even $l$ and equals $2q(d/2)^{\otimes l}$ for odd $l$; since $M^{(2)}=0$ and $\sum_kq_k|x_k|^2=qa^2+(-q)a^2=0$, the traceless quadrupole $Q_{ij}=3M_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\sum_kq_k|x_k|^2$ vanishes, at the chosen chart origin. Here $Q=0$ but $p=qd$ is generally nonzero. By [[pthm-em-moment-origin-change]] (d), the quadrupole at reference point b is $-3(b_i p_j+b_jp_i)+2(b\cdot p)\delta_{ij}$; hence it is not generally origin invariant. If $q=0$, all moments and the potential vanish and the invariance special case holds ([[def-finite-sum]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). For (c), apply the twice-fundamental-theorem remainder computation to each of the two kernels directly, since the density theorem does not apply to the pair. Write $h_y(s):=|x-sy|^{-1}$ for $y\in\{d/2,-d/2\}$; for $r\ge2a$ and $s\in[0,1]$ one has $|x-sy|\ge r-a\ge r/2$, the chain rule gives $h_y'(s)=\frac{(x-sy)\cdot y}{|x-sy|^3}$ and $h_y''(s)=-\frac{|y|^2}{|x-sy|^3}+3\frac{((x-sy)\cdot y)^2}{|x-sy|^5}$ with $|h_y''(s)|\le4|y|^2/|x-sy|^3\le32|y|^2/r^3=32a^2/r^3$, and the identity $h_y(1)-h_y(0)-h_y'(0)=\int_0^1(1-t)h_y''(t)\,dt$ is the fundamental theorem applied to $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl[(1-t)h_y'(t)+h_y(t)\bigr]=(1-t)h_y''(t)$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), so $h_y(1)=1/r+x\cdot y/r^3+R_y(x)$ with $|R_y(x)|\le16|y|^2/r^3$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Substituting the two kernels with their charges and using $|y|=a$, with the two linear terms adding to $q(x\cdot d)/r^3=p\cdot x/r^3$,
$$\varphi(x)-\frac{p\cdot x}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\bigl(R_{d/2}(x)-R_{-d/2}(x)\bigr),\qquad \Bigl|\varphi(x)-\frac{p\cdot x}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}\Bigr|\le\frac{|q|(16a^2+16a^2)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}=\frac{32|q|a^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}=\frac{8|q|a^2}{\pi\varepsilon_0r^3},$$
which is (c); reading it against [[pthm-em-electric-dipole-expansion]] gives (d). The two vector terms use the Euclidean inner product and norm ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]); no differentiation of $\varphi$ beyond the off-pole gradient is used and no value at the poles is asserted. For (e), no field energy is computed and the self-energy of a point charge is not claimed finite here. Countable Choice is used only through the cited distribution and Lebesgue interfaces; the potential and field of each charge are the idealised singular objects of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) and [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e). The h_y parameter remainder is a continuous finite Riemann integral: its bound may use [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] on [0,1]. All volume/source Lebesgue estimates instead use the nonnegative-integral rules. This distinguishes the actual Darboux use from the Lebesgue uses.

items.physical_scope: The exact potential of two ideal stationary point charges of opposite sign, its distributional equations, its source moments ($Q=0$, $p=qd$, vanishing traceless quadrupole) and an explicit far-field remainder bound of order $a^2/r^3$ about the ideal-dipole potential. The source is singular; no self-energy, self-force, dynamics, bound-state, stability or empirical claim is made.
